subject: PO vs Card \u0014 procurement readiness & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@finopsco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: PO vs Card  procurement readiness & next steps

Hi Priya 

Great to meet you and Tom on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Redwood fits your performance and security requirements. We covered Dedicated vs Hosted briefly  you indicated Hosted will work for now while you complete vendor onboarding.
- Two procurement constraints you mentioned: centralized AP requires a PO for new vendors, and the platform only allows payment by ACH/PO until vendor is fully onboarded in your marketplace (FinOps Marketplace).

Proposed next steps: 
1) I can share a short vendor onboarding checklist and SOW draft for your finance and legal review (attached).
2) If AP needs a PO-first flow, we can support invoicing on a monthly invoice tied to a PO  would you like us to surface a draft PO template?
3) If marketplace onboarding is preferred, we can align with Lauren to get the marketplace listing required fields filled so the procurement team can pay by card once approved (timeline typically 2-4 weeks).

Please let me know which path your AP prefers (PO on file vs card via marketplace) and any specific vendor onboarding blockers we should prep for. Happy to loop in our onboarding lead to accelerate.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: FinOpsCo_SOW_v1.pdf, vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx

From: Priya Sharma <priya@finopsco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finopsco.com>, AP Team <ap@finopsco.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 17:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO vs Card  procurement readiness & next steps

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the recap and the attachments  reviewed quickly with Tom. A few clarifications from AP: 

- Our standard is PO-first for any new vendor above $10k/yr. We can open a PO now but need an itemized invoice or SOW to tie to it.
- Card payments are allowed only after vendor onboarding is complete in our marketplace (we require the vendor to be in our vendor registry for card authorization).
- Onboarding checklist looks good. The main blocker is SOC 2 evidence and proof of data residency  legal will want those before we list you on the marketplace.

Could you do the following?
1) Send an itemized invoice/SOW we can attach to a PO (line items + monthly estimate).
2) Confirm whether Redwood can accept invoices via email to ap@finopsco.com and whether you can provide SOC 2/AICPA report or an alternative attestation.

If you can get those two things over, I can start the PO and loop in legal for the marketplace approval. Goal is to have PO in place within 7-10 business days if nothing blocks.

Best,
Priya
Head of Procurement, FinOpsCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@finopsco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finopsco.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO vs Card  procurement readiness & next steps

Thanks Priya  that's super helpful. Quick answers: 

- I've attached the SOW draft and an itemized monthly estimate (FinOpsCo_SOW_v1.pdf)  let me know if you'd like different granularity.
- Redwood can accept emailed invoices to ap@finopsco.com and also support EDI/Ariba if needed; we'll surface the billing contact details and remit instructions in the final SOW.
- For SOC 2 we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA; alternatively, we have a summary security package and an ISO-equivalent attestation we can share immediately. Data residency: we can commit to US-only region for your tenant and provide the audit logs needed for legal.

Lauren  can you please confirm the marketplace listing fields and typical time-to-approval so I can set expectations with Priya? Specifically: required company details, tax IDs, required security docs and contact email for marketplace ops.

Priya  if it helps, we can also provisionally accept a PO to reserve capacity and then follow up with marketplace onboarding so you can switch to card payments later.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@finopsco.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finopsco.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO vs Card  procurement readiness & next steps

Hi all 

Quick note from Marketplace Ops: typical approval timeline is 2-4 weeks after we receive the security docs (SOC 2 or equivalent), company legal name, W-9/Tax ID, and primary billing contact. Required fields are in the vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx I copied to Marissa (attached).

We can expedite to 7-10 business days if Priya's team can provisionally accept the PO so we can start the listing in parallel with legal review. Our Marketplace team will keep the vendor in pending status and enable card processing once approved.

Action items: 
- Marissa: finalize invoice/SOW and provide SOC 2 summary or NDA for report delivery (ASAP).
- Priya/AP: confirm whether you want us to send a draft PO template to attach to your PO, and confirm billing email (ap@finopsco.com is fine).

Happy to join a short sync if helpful.

Best,
Lauren
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
